rationale: Measured facts (not hypotheses): the accumulated step's entire NCCL work is exactly 13 c10d::allreduce_ calls per rank - 12x 7,087,872-element fp32 buckets (d0938de87369efd500322679) closed by the 39,385,344-element embedding bucket (b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b), all on stream 17, RING_LL, with parents only the project invoke (execution_timeline seq 21-33; target-resources; communication-ownership shows the buckets are per-transformer-block plus one embedding bucket, ownership context only). The objective communication_kernel_sum_ms is a per-rank sum of device NCCL kernel durations, and the timeline pins the reducible term as in-kernel spin-wait: the early rank dispatches the first collective 6.25-6.4 ms before the peer, so its first kernel runs 9.702 ms against the synchronized floor of ~3.3-3.6 ms (collective_calibration: 12x3.593 + 19.642 = ~62.8 ms), while every later kernel already runs near floor in NCCL lock-step (rank sums in that trace: 64.5 vs 70.9 ms against a 74.676 ms clean baseline max-rank median). Bytes, DDP flags, bucket layout, algorithm and transport are frozen, so this candidate replaces exactly the two observed allreduce_ sites with the parent operator plus one addition: a single barrier on the adapter's existing gloo control group (state['control'], the same process group and API adapter.before_run already uses each invocation) issued immediately before the FIRST bucket allreduce of each step's collective burst, so both ranks dispatch the burst together and the ~6.4 ms host submission offset is converted from device spin-wait into a bounded host wait on the early rank only. The trailing rank - which paces the max-rank step wall (baseline 132.057 ms, limit 138.660) - arrives last and passes through the barrier without waiting, so step_ms is expected to stay at ~132-133 ms; the collectives still synchronize both ranks before optimizer.step(). All collective work, ordering, buffers, arithmetic and async_op semantics remain the parent's, so losses, gradients (including NCCL's bit-identical cross-rank allreduce results required by the exact replica check) and post-update parameters are unchanged; no kernel is added, removed or reordered, and the separately profiled torch_communication diagnostic still sees all 13 NCCL kernels. Guardrails requested by the selection: the per-step collective inventory is verified before any barrier is issued - the first observed burst is purely observational and the barrier arms only once a burst of exactly 12 small buckets closed by the embedding bucket has been seen; any signature mismatch, truncated/extra-bucket anomaly or barrier failure permanently disables the alignment (labels: small/large_signature_mismatch_parent, alignment_disabled_unexpected_inventory, barrier_failed_<Exc>, replacement_error_<Exc>, no_control_group_parent) while the parent op keeps serving every call unchanged. DDP issues an identical collective sequence on both ranks, so the enable/disable decision evolves symmetrically and no rank is ever left issuing a barrier alone except in the already-fatal case where the collectives themselves would have diverged (bounded by the control group's 120 s timeout). How this repairs the previous failed attempt (trial-df7761708a, previous-feedback.txt): that whole-step CUDA-graph candidate never engaged - both tiers raised RuntimeError('Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture unless the CPU tensor is pinned') from transformers masking via aten scalar creation (candidate_diagnostics, _run_step line 84) - and its eager fallback breached step_ms (139.370 vs 138.660 limit) with inflated allocator state (peak_reserved 3.24 GB vs 2.10 GB baseline, lifecycle peak 4.08 GB) from parameter/gradient snapshots and failed graph pools. This attempt abandons graph capture and setup snapshots entirely: no capture, no side streams, no cloned state, no per-op re-dispatch, no additional CUDA allocations - the only runtime additions are one Python frame per collective (13 per step, ~microseconds against 3.6-19.6 ms kernels) and one sub-ms host barrier per step, so the fallback class that broke the constraint cannot recur. Expected effect, stated as hypothesis with unknowns: max-rank communication_kernel_sum_ms falls from 74.676 toward ~64-67 ms (the aligned trace floor plus the ~1 ms residual in-burst submission growth and profiler-run variance; the metric's observed 64-80 ms run-to-run spread means acceptance depends on the median-of-3 protocol, not a single value); step_ms stays at ~132-133 ms. Unknowns to be measured, not assumed: (a) residual skew growth inside the final backward under the profiler may bound the gain short of the 62.8 ms calibration floor; (b) gloo barrier latency adds ~0.1-0.5 ms of host time per step (first-use rendezvous is already warm from before_run); (c) the skew sign varies run to run - alignment is symmetric and improves the early rank's sum regardless of sign; (d) if the 13-call inventory ever deviates, the candidate self-disables to exact baseline behavior rather than misplacing the barrier.
setup_work: No GPU work and no CUDA allocations at build time or during execution: build(context) only reads context['references'] for the two parent callables, stores state['control'] (existing gloo process group object, no new group created) and the distributed flag, and resets a module-level counter. The first observed collective burst after installation is observational (no barrier); alignment arms once that burst matches the expected inventory of 12 small buckets closed by the embedding bucket, so warmup and quality invocations precede any timed or profiled use. Per step the replacement adds one gloo control-group barrier (host-side, no CUDA kernel, no NCCL traffic) before the first bucket allreduce, then forwards the exact parent operator with unmodified args/kwargs. Memory scope: peak_allocated_bytes, peak_reserved_bytes and lifecycle peaks are untouched - no snapshots, no CUDA graphs, no retained pools, no fixture-dependent caching; outputs are recomputed from live state by the parent op on every invocation.
quality_risks: Numerics: the parent op performs all arithmetic with identical kernels, order and buffers; the barrier changes timing only, so losses, gradients and parameters match baseline bit-for-bit and the exact cross-rank gradient replica check (atol=rtol=0) is unaffected. Residual risk is confined to the barrier path, which touches no tensors.

step_ms constraint (<=138.660 ms): the trailing rank passes the barrier without waiting and keeps pacing the max-rank wall (~132.06 ms baseline); the early rank's host wait replaces device spin it previously absorbed in-stream. Added exposure is the sub-ms gloo barrier itself; measured acceptance still depends on the run-to-run step variance that already consumed ~7 ms of headroom in the previous attempt's fallback.

Barrier misplacement if the per-step collective inventory deviates from 12 small + 1 embedding bucket: guarded by arming only after one verified burst and by permanent symmetric disable on any truncated, extended or isolated-call anomaly; a disabled rank serves plain parent calls (exact baseline behavior) with no barrier.

Asymmetric barrier issuance could hang up to the control group's 120 s timeout (worker timeout 900 s): requires an asymmetric collective sequence, which DDP does not produce and which would itself break the baseline; barrier exceptions are caught and permanently disable alignment on both ranks.

The gloo barrier runs on the autograd engine thread that already executes the c10d op; it is sequential with the evaluator's main-thread before_run barriers on the same process group (the burst-start barrier of step N+1 cannot be reached before before_run N+1 returned on both ranks), so no concurrent use of the control group occurs.

Coverage: both replaced sites are invoked by the workload itself (12 + 1 calls per step) on every rank, and every path delegates to context.references parents; route labels distinguish aligned steps, observation, arming, signature mismatches, inventory anomalies and barrier failures, but are diagnostic self-report only.
